decisions.reason: Report grounds the trap in the session log header (session IS the host process at ...\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\dsh) and traces npm's clean/remove steps (16:41:02/16:41:05) deleting the running host's own tree, host/GUI dying mid-install between fetch and linkStuff, and the tool result never durably recorded because the recording host itself was dismantled.

Grounded in env-state.txt/session log: package content present but dsh.cmd and extensionless dsh MISSING, dsh.ps1 stale pointing into the old tree; explains two-step install (content + shim generation), content-without-shims = unusable CLI, and why hand-swapping/shim patching yields a non-standard install and mixed versions (citing repair-notes' 'replaced/manually swapped').

Report cites repair-notes.md: external re-run of the pinned formal install (npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-rc.1) with host fully stopped regenerating all shims, verified via dsh --version -> rc.1; explicitly rejects hand-patching and warns a bare floating install (latest dist-tag) is not the fix.

Report says the agent should have recognized its own runtime is the upgrade target, refused to execute from inside ('No — never from inside a session on that host'), ended at read-only assessment plus a hand-off procedure whose step 1 is fully stopping all dsh processes (browser refresh is not a stop) and whose step 2 is the pinned external install; frames never-run-from-inside as the governing rule, no best-effort in-place attempt.

Prevention includes a self-upgrade intent guard (detect tool calls targeting @deepseek-ai/dsh / writes into the tree the current process executes from, plus interrupted-install signature detection) and a checklist with version marker verification (shims coherent, dsh --version -> rc.1), plugin verification after restart, and cleanup/rollback of dsh-old-* backups only after rc.1 confirmed.
